rows.accepted_scope: For N≥2 and a supplied primitive Nth root, the two exact Weyl equations force M=cF; scalar calibration forces c=1. Over complex numbers the joint Frobenius residual gap is exactly 2 sin(π/N). For a fixed calibrated linear map over F_q with stacked defect rank ρ, h independent uniform probes accept with exact probability q^(−hρ), using 1+3h candidate calls.
rows.proof_review: The first relation recursively fixes column j to D^j times column zero. The second makes its row amplitudes constant. Conjugating by unitary F yields commutators whose orthogonal Weyl-basis weights are |1−ω^a|²+|1−ω^b|². The first positive eigenvalue is 4sin²(π/N); FD attains equality. The common probe lies in the intersection kernel of the two defects, hence q^(N−ρ) accepted vectors.
qualifications: The residual bound is distance to the scalar Fourier family, with separate calibration. Its gap decays with N.
Exact acceptance probability is conditional on passing the deterministic calibration; a wrong scalar rejects there. The algorithm is not a linearity or adaptive/stateful-oracle test.
Field/root and any normalization square-root preparation are separate; norm statements are complex. Modular rejection transfers only under valid coefficient specialization and nonzero denominators.
rows.overlay_review: P05/S5 is a distinct accepted negative certification theorem: finite projective Weyl orbits of any finite probe set admit a continuous invariant distance interpolant f, giving A(x)=exp(iπf([x]))Ux, agreeing on all tested scalar/Weyl orbits and equaling −Ux on another orbit. It neither contradicts the fixed-linear theorem nor supplies a probabilistic/runtime lower bound for a specified implementation class.
remaining_obligations: No candidate transform or uniform parameter synthesis is supplied; any positive certification must establish the promised function class.

rows.accepted_scope: For normalized complex Fourier U and invertible M, one inverse row of support s gives ||M−U||₂≥sqrt(1−s/N). A commutator rank budget r<N gives cos((2 floor(r/2)+1)π/(2N)). For columns supported on at most 1≤s<N sites, the sharp Weyl defect floor is 2sin(π/[2(s+1)]). The current local inverse-neighborhood spectral-quantile theorem and exact infimum/attainment boundaries are accepted separately.
rows.proof_review: The one-row bound follows from bM=e_i and |(bU)_i|≤sqrt(s/N)||b||, completing a square. Fourier commutator singular values follow from the distinct roots of (D*Z)^N=(−1)^(N−1)I and best rank-r approximation. Zeros cut a sparse column into Dirichlet paths; the longest permitted path gives the sine eigenvalue. For H=M⁻¹ and B[I,Jᶜ]=0, local rank ρ gives d=|I|−ρ supported vectors carried by M* into I. Minimax yields error²≥1−σ_d(U[J,I])². Complementary inverse-block nullity gives the same result.
qualifications: The catalogue sparse-column summary must retain 1≤s<N. At s=N a Weyl eigenvector has zero defect, contradicting the displayed positive constant if used without that guard.
The commutator rank budget is architecture-specific; fixed common frames matter. Fourier commutator rank is N for even N, N−1 for odd N.
Current scalar bounds require integer s≥1: r=0 uses sqrt(1−s/N); r≥1 uses sqrt(max(0,1−4sr/N)). At s=0 invertibility forces full-rank defect and only zero is universal.
Single-neighborhood sharpness allows unrestricted other entries. It is not exact support-union attainment or globally sharp uniform row sparsity.
rows.overlay_review: For 0≤r<t=|I|, d=t−r, class {M invertible: rank(M⁻¹[I,Jᶜ])≤r} is empty if d>|J|. Otherwise optimum/infimum equals sqrt(1−σ_d(U[J,I])²). If σ_d>0, M=U−QQ*U P_Ic attains it and is invertible. If σ_d=0, every feasible M has error>1, while scaled feasible permutations approach 1. If r≥t, constraint is automatic and error zero is attainable. For 4|N, one-sided parity support has exact correction-rank cutoff N/4. Positive-integer-rank scalar envelope is equivalent, not stronger, than the 4sr/N expression.
remaining_obligations: Worldwide priority and a sharp theorem for global uniform row sparsity remain unestablished; no field operator norm transfer is licensed.

rows.proof_review: Averaging W*XW with X=U*M gives tr(X)I/N; expand the commutator square. Four-phase fourth moments equal (tr H)²+tr(H²)−ΣH_ii². Residual Frobenius norm ≤2τ gives E Z²≤8τ⁴. A seed error δ0 gives ||M−U||₂≤δ0+2τ. Complementary inverse-block nullity equates a Green cross rank to its weighted cycle crossings; product cross ranks add only in a consistently tracked frame.

For N=2m with m odd, the parity Fourier block has singular values 1/sqrt(2); do not use this as the same full-rank parity statement when 4|N.
Stochastic small loss is not exact equality or an optimization convergence/uniform synthesis theorem. Seed correction can leave the original Green grammar and must be charged in general cuts.

rows.accepted_scope: For N≥2 over C, legal ungauged (I−αS^ε−βT^δ)⁻¹ signed families span N² dimensions for odd N and N²−1 for even N, omitting (N/2,N/2). Fourier belongs exactly when 4 does not divide N. Nearest-neighbor path sums with arbitrary diagonal masks require total path Green-stage count at least floor(N/2), using a genuine partition.
rows.proof_review: Primitive q quantum-binomial collapse gives W^N=(α^N+β^N)I and inverse polynomial divided by Δ=1−α^N−β^N. All degree<N Gaussian coefficients are nonzero; polynomial independence on the legal complex open set spans each signed triangle. Four triangles cover all positions except the even central point. Its Fourier Gauss coefficient vanishes for N≡2 mod4 and is nonzero for 4|N. At a true contiguous partition each nearest-neighbor Green crosses with rank≤1; products and sums add ranks and the target has a consecutive-exponent Vandermonde block.
qualifications: Δ≠0 is essential; zero local diagonal pivots are legal if Δ≠0. Root/field/bit preparation and numerical conditioning are separate.
The span proof is over an infinite complex parameter domain, not a claim that every finite parameter field attains that span. Existential span does not give cheap coefficient synthesis.

Separated equal halves at odd N omit a middle coordinate and the source product-rank lemma is false; N=3 shear factors give zero factor cross blocks and a nonzero product cross block. Include the middle in the right partition.
Products, Weyl endpoint shifts, additional generators and long strides escape the ungauged span or nearest-neighbor grammar.
remaining_obligations: No full Fourier evaluator or efficient signed-family coefficient synthesis is established. The inherited literal +1 preparation-operation correction is retained, not rerun as implementation timing.

rows.proof_review: Expand (h+Ms)(t+Qu). The (s,t)|(h,u) flattening reduces by nonzero row/column scales and repeated rows/columns to a Q-by-M Vandermonde; the other paired cuts reduce to invertible Fourier products. Input/output flattening lower-bounds CP rank by N, and fixing (t,u) supplies N four-leg rank-one terms. rows.accepted_scope: For supplied primitive Nth root, a nonempty Fourier rectangle is rank one exactly when N divides every row-difference times column-difference. Minimum disjoint rank-one endpoint-incidence cost is N min_(d|N)(d+N/d). This is 2N^(3/2) for squares and N(N+1) for primes.
rows.proof_review: All 2×2 minors vanish exactly under the divisibility test. If H is generated by row differences and |H|=d, rows lie in one H coset and columns in one annihilator coset of size N/d. Consequently a+b≥(ab/N) min(d+N/d). Disjoint areas sum to N²; the N full coset-product tiles attain the bound. Complex higher-rank endpoint-cost bound follows from rank≥ab/N and r≥1.
qualifications: Incidence cost refers to independent tile contractions or specified dense rank factors. Shared Cooley–Tukey computations are outside that accounting.
Prime higher-rank full-minor claims are characteristic-zero. Complex norm arguments do not transfer to finite fields.

Literal source tiled loop adds zero once per tile without charging it, producing N extra additions; direct first-term initialization realizes its stated circuit ledger. MILP status is not an exact proof certificate.
remaining_obligations: Higher-rank incidence optimum for general nonsquare composite N and worldwide priority remain open; ordinary two-axis FFT is not a new speedup.

rows.accepted_scope: For a four-QS-stage word S4 P3 S3 Q S2 P1 S1 and unshifted Q:j↦3j mod N with gcd(3,N)=1, qs(S3 Q S2 Q⁻¹)≤r3+5r2. rows.proof_review: Each membership boundary contributes at most r to a QS cross block. For unshifted multiplication by a, the preimage of a prefix has at most a intervals and contains zero, so Γ≤2a−1; multiplication adds QS orders. Three-stage expansion through an output prefix/input cyclic interval leaves a separated middle block. Average over all wrapping cyclic intervals to obtain exact Wt/N, retaining endpoint order budgets. The named cutoff dependency supplies explicit bit-reversal rectangle discrepancy D_k=k/3+1/9−(−1)^k/(9·2^k)>9 for k≥27.
qualifications: The sharper (2b−1)r interval bound requires an included endpoint; arbitrary b intervals only guarantee 2br. Affine shifts may lose that endpoint improvement.

Natural/diagonal Fourier endpoints work; one endpoint may be affine with unit multiplier while the opposite is arbitrarily permuted. Both arbitrary permutations require complex prime full spark, not dyadic/composite transfer.
The explicit cutoff is conservative, not an optimal finite threshold. Arbitrary middle permutations and general circuits are not covered.
remaining_obligations: Gray-middle and other unbounded-fragmentation families are outside this collapse; a necessary-cut survivor is not a coefficient-compatible construction.

rows.proof_review: Boundary decomposition gives both cross ranks≤d_N r. Track net whole-group swap parity through products and add rank contributions. For odd k use the middle bit; for even k use agreement of the middle two bits. Outer small Fourier transforms reduce all four target half-blocks to nonzero scalars or invertible 2×2 primitive-fourth-root blocks, hence rank N/2. Bit reversal preserves these groups.

rows.accepted_scope: If inverse factors are row-d_j-sparse plus rank-r_j defects, the full inverse is row-Πd_j-sparse plus rank≤Σr_j error, even with monomial interfaces. Exact Fourier requires Σr_j≥floor(N/(1+Πd_j)). Separately, moving QS partitions obey the weighted boundary-rank inequality; repeated rotl(bitrev) has the stated square-root depth gates.
rows.proof_review: Telescope the product difference around the product of sparse baselines. Each error term has rank≤r_j and row support degrees multiply. In floor(N/(k+1)) consecutive Fourier rows, a row-k-sparse comparison touches at most mk columns, leaving m zero columns and a full Vandermonde minor. For moving cuts transport the subset through each declared new-to-old interface permutation; boundary contributions add without requiring an invariant subset. Binary transition counts follow by trailing-one classes. Twisted central witnesses reduce to invertible 2×2/four-consecutive-row 4×4 Fourier blocks.
qualifications: For deriving sparse inverse baselines from a sum, every reference/endpoint must meet the invertibility and shared-reference hypotheses and c_j=Σc_js≠0. Counting individual sparse Green denominators inside arbitrary sums does not establish sparse total inverse.
Fixed bounded correction ranks yield t≥log₂N−O(log log N) for degree-two references; this is a representation depth result.
Twisted reversal is distinct from ordinary repeated bit reversal: four QS1 stages fail from N=64, versus N=128 for the ordinary central witness.
Source Weyl character packets require α≠0 for exact support counts/N-dimensional span; α=0 gives only identity. That side result is not recounted as new work here.
remaining_obligations: N=256 cut-feasible mixing survivor still lacks Fourier coefficients. Rank-distant multi-order sums, arbitrary routes and shared evaluators are not excluded by this common-reference theorem.

rows.accepted_scope: For N=2^k (k≥1), m=2^floor(k/2), q=N/m, let L count paired layers, each a sum of weighted Green terms in the two cycles Z and RZR, with monomial endpoints preserving bank blocks (or at least striped classes). Arbitrary same-bank block-diagonal matrices may be inserted. Exact natural Fourier requires L(q/2+m)≥N/2, hence L≥ceil(N/(q+2m)). Three paired layers fail from N=128; four from N=256. The separate fixed area-balanced/complement two-stage diagonal-middle grid grammar fails at every dyadic grid side M≥8.
rows.proof_review: The even-bank/odd-bank Fourier rectangle becomes a direct sum of Vandermonde blocks because q/2 divides m. Its rank is N/2. Natural and bit-reversed cycle incoming counts are q/2 and m. Complementary inverse-block ranks equal those sparse crossing ranks, sums add and products add, while same-bank factors contribute zero. The separate area downset has ≤2M frontier vertices and overlap h=|B∩ρ(B)|, giving two-stage rank≤2h+4M. All five base cuts are replayed by literal topological reachability; exact rational lens-area bounds prove the tail from M=256.
qualifications: Clarify the catalogue phrase “L weighted Green occurrences”: the sharp displayed budget and thresholds count paired layers, not individual Green summands. The theorem source states this explicitly.
The N=128 four-paired-layer capacity equals 64 and does not exclude a construction there. At N=256 capacity 96<128.
Arbitrary bank routing, independent cycles, and endpoint permutations mixing stripes are outside the striped theorem.

The companion area route ρ(i)=N−1−i is coordinate complement, not bit reversal. Its diagonal-middle theorem is separate; a middle monomial needs c≥N/4−2h−4M crossings but this necessity is not sufficient.
remaining_obligations: No sharp universal route threshold or coefficient construction follows. Companion finite certificates M=2,4 are nonexcluded and are not claimed impossible.
